pages.text: A main building — hatchery, command center or nexus — placed from a spawn egg founds your base: 50 minerals and 4 workers. One base per dimension, shared by all three races.

A map ringed with 8 armor shards of a race makes its $(l)resource crate$(), your base's store that opens from its top. Without a base, the $(l)summoning beacon$() of a crate calls a worker: see $(l)Summoning Beacon$().

Nine mineral shards make a $(l)block of minerals$() (and back). It is mined like an ore, by hand, pickaxe or worker, but it is not broken: each time it gives a shard and keeps the rest, nine times. $(l)Rich minerals$(), gold, lie rarely deep in the stone: two shards a time.

Workers bring what they gather to the nearest $(l)storage$(): a main building. They take $(l)minerals first$(); only where there are none other valuable blocks. Take it out where they brought it: right-click the main building and it opens like a chest — minerals show as mineral shards; anything valuable laid in turns into minerals by its worth. (Supply platforms of older worlds still keep their bank.)
Units and buildings cost only $(l)minerals and vespene$(), as in StarCraft II. Build the main building with a worker when you have its price.
